The work-environment response pins Doc-Lineage's build order as identity → extraction → ledger schemas → **lineage and comparison engine** ([INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md §D, consultant-report comparison tool; §Scope fixed 2026-09-04](https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md)). The consultant tracker already names the segment vocabulary (`VERBATIM / NEAR_VERBATIM / REVISED / NEW / DROPPED`) and materiality tiers (`T1` decision-relevant, `T2` factual refresh, `T3` cosmetic) as **data fields**, not ad hoc branches ([response §D, consultant-report comparison tool](https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md)). The communication synthesis tool documents a costly failure mode: inferring an exit from document silence produced a wrong finding — **silence is weak evidence, never proof of removal** ([response §D, communication synthesis tool](https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md)). **Latent fragility, not a current break:** issues #2–#4 define prerequisites; this issue delivers the engine they feed.

## Scope

Implement the comparison/lineage engine in Doc-Lineage after #2 (identity), #3 (extraction), and #4 (ledger schemas):

1. Segment classification into `VERBATIM`, `NEAR_VERBATIM`, `REVISED`, `NEW`, `DROPPED` with `T1`/`T2`/`T3` tiers loaded from versioned data files (not `if tier == "T1"` code branches).
2. Document-family detection and supersession chains (filename-prefix supersession from Q9, content-hash identity from #2).
3. A **silence-is-weak-evidence** invariant: absence of a mention must never auto-emit `DROPPED` or an exit inference without an explicit positive signal.
4. A synthetic corpus generator with labeled ground truth so the engine can be evaluated in CI without proprietary documents.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT implement HTML/Word/PPTX rendering (Deliverable-Render owns outputs).
- Do NOT re-implement PDF extraction or OCR (depends on #3).
- Do NOT invent new ledger field names (depends on #4 schemas).
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a green `pytest` run that collected **0** of the named comparison/lineage tests is a failure. The deliberate-break acceptance criteria below must be demonstrated.

- [ ] Add `src/doc_lineage/lineage/families.py` with `detect_family(doc: DocumentRef) -> FamilyId` and `build_supersession_chain(docs: Sequence[DocumentRef]) -> list[SupersessionEdge]` using content-hash identity from #2 and numeric-prefix supersession heuristics described in [response §C Q9](https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md).
- [ ] Add `src/doc_lineage/compare/silence.py` with `apply_silence_invariant(classified: ClassifiedSegment, *, prior_mentions: int) -> ClassifiedSegment` that refuses to map bare absence to `DROPPED` (returns `UNKNOWN_ABSENCE` or leaves unclassified per schema).

With this change, `tests/compare/test_silence_invariant.py::test_absence_does_not_emit_dropped` **must FAIL**. Revert the edit after capturing the failure.

## Why

The tracked-variable schema for this repo does not need to be invented. Two comparison tools already run in the work environment with real, named field sets, and the response gives them verbatim (section D). Adopting those names is what makes a tool built here interoperable with the tools already in use there; inventing parallel names is the single change most likely to make this repo useless.

Evidence: response section D, the consultant-report comparison tool and the legal-document lineage tool (https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md).

## Scope

A schema module plus JSON Schema files for the record types those two tools already emit, expressed once so both a consultant-report comparison and a legal-document comparison populate the same shapes.

## Non-Goals

- No renaming for elegance. Where the existing tools have a field name, that name wins even if a better one exists.
- No comparison logic in this issue. Schema and validation only.
- No new materiality judgments. The tier vocabularies are adopted as data, not re-derived.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `src/doc_lineage/schema/change_ledger.py` with fields `doc_type, transition, canonical_section, subsection, item, page_new, change_type, tier, topic, prior_text, current_text`.
- [ ] Add `continuity_ledger` with `doc_type, transition, canonical_section, status, words_current, carry_forward_pct, refresh_pct, verbatim_words, near_verbatim_words, revised_words, new_words, dropped_words, segments_verbatim, segments_near, segments_revised, segments_new, segments_dropped, segments_cosmetic, new_items, dropped_items`.
- [ ] Add `persistence_ledger` with `doc_type, canonical_section, item, consecutive_years_unchanged, first_seen, last_seen, words, text`, and `stale_flag_ledger` as that shape plus `report_year, flag`.
- [ ] Add `section_crosswalk` with `doc_type, year, raw_section, canonical_section, words`.
- [ ] Add `material_ledger` with the legal tool's seven columns `date, tier, theme, category, change, from_value, to_value`, documenting that `from` and `to` are reserved words in Python and that the wire names stay `From` and `To`.
- [ ] Define the segment classification vocabulary as a closed enumeration `VERBATIM, NEAR_VERBATIM, REVISED, NEW, DROPPED`, and the materiality tiers as `T1` decision-relevant, `T2` factual refresh, `T3` cosmetic.
- [ ] Publish JSON Schema for each record type under `schemas/` and validate every fixture against it in tests.
- [ ] Add a round-trip test that a ledger row serializes to the wire names the existing tools use and parses back unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every field name listed above exists with that exact wire spelling, asserted by a test that reads the names from the JSON Schema rather than from Python identifiers.
- [ ] The segment vocabulary and tier set reject an unknown value rather than passing it through.
- [ ] A row with a non-finite number in any percentage or word-count field is rejected at validation, not stored.
- [ ] Fixtures exist for both a consultant-report transition and a legal-filing transition, and both validate.

## Test Gate

issues.body:
## Why

Three separate extraction implementations exist in the work environment today, each solving page pointers, content hashing and recognition fallback slightly differently, and the response names consolidating them as a systematization target. More sharply: **a real minority of legal documents are scanned images with no text layer**, and one recognition pass there recovered more than twenty documents and five hundred pages that every prior text-based analysis had silently skipped. An extraction library without a recognition stage produces coverage figures that are wrong rather than merely incomplete.

Evidence: response section C8 and the appendix entries on extraction and the recognition pipeline (https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md).

## Scope

One extraction library over PDF, Word and PowerPoint that returns text with a page pointer for every span, caches by content identity, and falls back to optical character recognition for pages with no text layer.

## Non-Goals

- No diffing, lineage or scoring. Extraction only.
- No cloud recognition service; the fallback runs locally.
- No dependency on the manifest file format beyond `stable_id`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `src/doc_lineage/extract/__init__.py` exposing `extract(path) -> Document`, where `Document` carries `stable_id` and a list of `Span(text, page, bbox, source)` with `source` in `text_layer | ocr`.
- [ ] Implement the PDF reader and detect absence of a text layer **per page**, not per document.
- [ ] Implement the recognition fallback per page, invoked only for pages whose text layer is absent, marking those spans `source="ocr"`.
- [ ] Handle rotated pages and diagonal watermark text explicitly; both are named as silent corruption sources in the response.
- [ ] Cache extracted text in a side store keyed by `stable_id` and page number, never by path.
- [ ] Report coverage per document as three counts reported together: `pages_with_text_layer`, `pages_recognized`, `pages_unreadable`.
- [ ] Add Word and PowerPoint readers returning the same `Span` shape with a paragraph or slide pointer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A synthetic image-only PDF yields spans with `source="ocr"` and a non-zero `pages_recognized`; the same document with recognition disabled reports `pages_unreadable` above zero rather than an empty success.
- [ ] A mixed PDF where one page lacks a text layer recognizes only that page; other pages report `source="text_layer"`.
- [ ] A rotated page's extracted text is in reading order, asserted against a committed expected string.
- [ ] Renaming the input file produces a cache hit rather than a re-extraction.
- [ ] No code path returns a coverage figure that omits the unreadable count.

## Test Gate

`tests/test_extract_coverage.py`, run by this repo's CI gate. Demonstrate it by deliberately breaking the fallback: make text-layer detection per-document instead of per-page, confirm the mixed-PDF test fails, revert, confirm it passes. Record both in the pull request.

## Implementation Notes

Keep the recognition dependency optional at import time so the text-layer path works without it, but make an absent recognition backend an explicit `pages_unreadable` outcome rather than a silent skip. Fixtures must be synthetic and small.

issues.title: Extraction with page pointers and a mandatory recognition fallback

issues.body:
## Why

The work environment's document library has **no stable document identifiers**. The filename is the de facto identifier, supersession is an ad hoc numeric-prefix convention, and one existing tool there already had to derive a content-hash identifier for recognized text because a path-based key silently orphaned its data whenever a document was renamed. Every downstream capability in this repo (extraction cache, lineage, comparison, evidence pointers) needs an identity that survives a rename and a re-supply.

Evidence: sections C9 and C10 of the work-environment response (https://github.com/stranske/Ready/blob/main/research-program/artifacts/work-bundle/INFORMATION-REQUEST-RESPONSE.md) and the scope section of this repo's README.

## Scope

An identity module plus a manifest over a folder tree shaped one directory per manager, then one per document category, with per-year subdirectories in places.

## Non-Goals

- No integration with any document-management system. The library is a synced folder tree; there is nothing to call.
- No optical character recognition, extraction or diffing here. Identity and manifest only.
- No proprietary inputs. Tests use synthetic documents committed under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `src/doc_lineage/identity.py` computing a document identity from content: `sha256` of the raw bytes, a `doc_key` of `{entity_slug}/{category}/{as_of}` parsed from path and filename, and a `stable_id` that prefers the content hash.
- [ ] Parse the numeric-filename-prefix supersession convention into an explicit `supersedes` field and record `supersession_evidence` naming which convention matched.
- [ ] Add `src/doc_lineage/manifest.py` writing `manifest.jsonl`, one row per document: `stable_id, sha256, path, entity_slug, category, as_of, received_at, bytes, mime, supersedes, text_layer` where `text_layer` is tri-state `present | absent | unknown`.
- [ ] Make manifest generation idempotent and incremental: an unchanged tree rewrites no rows, and a renamed file keeps its `stable_id` while its `path` updates.
- [ ] Add `scripts/build_manifest.py` as the operator entry point taking a root directory and an output path, with no network access.
- [ ] Commit a synthetic fixture tree covering at least three managers, two categories, one renamed document and one superseded document.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Renaming a fixture document changes its `path` and leaves its `stable_id` and `sha256` unchanged.
- [ ] A byte-identical copy at a second path resolves to the same `stable_id`, and the manifest records both paths without duplicating the identity.
- [ ] A numerically prefixed re-supply records `supersedes` pointing at the prior `stable_id`, with the matched convention named in `supersession_evidence`.
- [ ] `text_layer` is `unknown` rather than `present` when no check has run, so a later coverage figure cannot count unexamined documents as text-bearing.
- [ ] A second run over an unchanged tree produces a byte-identical manifest.

## Test Gate

`tests/test_identity_manifest.py`, run by this repo's existing CI gate. Demonstrate the gate by deliberately breaking it: derive `stable_id` from `path` instead of content, confirm the rename test fails, revert, confirm it passes. Record both outcomes in the pull request.

## Implementation Notes

Standard library only for hashing and directory walking. `text_layer` must default to `unknown`; one sentinel meaning both "not checked" and "no text" is precisely the defect this repo cannot afford, because a real minority of legal documents there have no text layer and were silently excluded from every prior analysis (response section C8).
